results.bound: \mathrm{log}_2(\Gamma(\frac{\ell(n-\ell)}{n}+1)) \text{ queries; in particular } \mathrm{log}_2(\Gamma(\frac{k}{(k+1)^2}\cdot n+1)) \text{ for degree } k
results.quote: The query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least \(\mathrm{log}_2(\Gamma(\frac{\ell(n-\ell)}{n}+1))\). In particular, the complexity is at least \(\mathrm{log}_2(\Gamma(\frac{k}{(k+1)^2}\cdot n+1))\) where k denotes the degree of T.
For binary trees T with n leaves, the query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least \(\mathrm{log}_2(n!)-O(\log n)\).
The query complexity of inversion minimization on T is at least \(\mathrm{log}_2(n!)-O(k\mathrm{log}k)\).

Counting cross inversions from a set A of size a to a set B of size \(b\ge a\) with respect to a ranking \(\rho\) of \(X\doteq A\sqcup B\) requires \(\Omega((a+b)\mathrm{log}(a))\) queries in the comparison-query model, as does inversion minimization on the tree of Figure 2.

results.problem: Inversion minimization on trees of degree \le k
results.quote: Let T be a tree with \(\mathrm{deg}(T)\le k\). The query complexity of \(\Pi_T\) for bounded-error randomized algorithms is \(\Omega(\frac{n\mathrm{log}(n/k)}{k\mathrm{log}(k)})\).
Using this subroutine for computing MinRInv, we can improve the time complexity of our basic algorithm to \(O((\text{deg}(T)^22^{\text{deg}(T)}+\text{deg}(T)\cdot d_\text{avg}(T))\cdot n)\).

results.previous_best: O(\mathrm{log} n\mathrm{loglog} n) \text{ for general graphs}
results.quote: Adapting this algorithm for minimizing inversions in trees produces an approximation factor of \(O(\mathrm{log}(\mathrm{deg}(T))\mathrm{loglog}(\mathrm{deg}(T)))\) for \(\mathrm{MinInv}(T,\rho)\).
